title: The Ninth Dryer
hook: The all-night laundromat has nine dryers. The ninth has a sign: if it's ever running, don't open it.
lines: The all-night laundromat on Elm Street has nine dryers... and only eight of them work.
Number nine has a sign taped to its door, in thick black marker.
Out of order. If it's ever running... don't open it. Don't even look inside.
I do my laundry there on Thursdays, after midnight, when it's empty.
For a whole year, number nine just sat there. Cold. Silent. Dark.
Then last Thursday, while I was folding towels... it started to spin.
No coins. No plug. Just a slow, heavy tumble. Thump... thump... thump.
Like something soft and heavy, rolling over and over in the dark.
I kept folding. I didn't look. Then the thumping stopped.
And very slowly... from the inside... the little round door began to open.
I ran. I left everything behind. My basket. My towels. Even my keys.
My landlord let me in the next morning. Nothing was missing.
Then I opened my bedroom closet. My towels were in there... folded, and still warm.
And taped to the inside of the closet door, in thick black marker... Out of order.
